key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomer theory links mesogen order and network deformation to explain reversible actuation, soft elasticity, and domain-mediated mechanical responses.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports constitutive modeling of liquid crystal elastomer actuators and compliant structures with programmable, stimuli-responsive deformation.
method: Bridge anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics to neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Analyze stress-free ground states and stripe-domain accommodation of soft deformation.
Apply quasi-convex relaxation to classify three macroscopic response regimes in polydomain elastomers.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and three-phase response classification, but reports no experimental datasets or quantitative validation metrics.
watch_item: The ideal model assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; realistic predictions may require nonideality, director-gradient, and viscoelastic corrections.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
